methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: ‘Shaping our future’: Company powering AI data centers invests $50+ million in Henrico, adding 200 jobs - WWBT
signals.signal_reading: A $50M+ investment in AI infrastructure and 200 jobs in Henrico signals Richmond's emergence as a secondary concentration hub for AI capability, but the capital-intensive data center model produces concentrated economic benefit rather than distributed AI fluency across the region.

signals.title: Extra Credit: Roanoke College launches AI program for professionals
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's professional AI program represents intentional skill-building infrastructure outside traditional tech hubs, creating potential for distributed deep capability if graduates apply learning locally rather than migrate to metros.

signals.title: VA uses hundreds of AI systems. Veterans may not know when they’re involved. - Military Times
signals.signal_reading: The VA's deployment of hundreds of opaque AI systems affecting veterans without their knowledge signals shallow, non-participatory adoption that neither builds user capability nor distributes AI literacy—a pattern that could replicate across public services statewide.

signals.title: Virginia's best-paying jobs are most exposed to AI, report says - Axios
signals.signal_reading: High-wage jobs facing greatest AI exposure concentrates both opportunity and risk in already-advantaged metro corridors, where workers have resources to adapt, while lower-wage regions lack both exposure to AI transformation and resources to prepare for it.

signals.title: Virginia ranks fifth in workplace AI adoption, new report finds - WVIR
signals.signal_reading: Virginia's fifth-place workplace AI adoption ranking likely reflects platform-layer tool usage distributed across sectors rather than deep technical capability, signaling broad but shallow engagement that doesn't fundamentally shift the state's innovation capacity.
